# Flow intake

Intake decides what enters the committed workflow and in what shape. Everything downstream inherits these
answers. A vague criterion at intake becomes rework at validation (K §4, §5.1).

## Demand types (K §3.2)

capability · defect · security · reliability · dependency or toolchain · technical debt · discovery ·
compliance · developer experience · incident follow-up

Use the exact spelling that `work-items/TEMPLATE.md` uses.

## Shaping decisions (K §3.3)

Record exactly one of these, with the reason:

| Decision | When |
|---|---|
| Accept | The outcome and beneficiary are clear, and the item fits the service definition in brief §16 |
| Clarify | The outcome, beneficiary, or success signal is missing. List the questions and who can answer them |
| Combine | It duplicates or overlaps an existing card. Name the card |
| Reject | It does not support current goals, or brief §3 non-goals exclude it. Say which |
| Redirect | Another service owns it (brief §16). Name that service |
| Split | It will not fit the SLE. Propose the vertical slices |
| Discovery first | Uncertainty cannot be resolved cheaply. Propose a discovery card, and state that implementation waits |

## Acceptance criteria (K §8.2, §17.7)

- Write each criterion as observable behavior: Given a context, When an action happens, Then an outcome
  follows, And a side effect or signal where relevant.
- Give each criterion an ID (`AC1`, `AC2`, and so on) and a **Verified by** entry. The entry is a test
  path to be written, a manual step, a dashboard, or a release check.
- Cover failure and edge behavior: invalid input, absent dependencies, limits, timeouts, and concurrency
  when it applies.
- Include telemetry or documentation when they are part of the outcome.
- "Create a struct" and "add a module" are not criteria, except in an explicitly internal refactoring.
- Every number needs a source (brief §13), or a label marking it as an assumption.

Weak and strong forms:

```text
Weak:   The parser handles bad input.
Strong: AC3 — Given an expression nested 129 levels deep, when it is evaluated, then the tool prints
        "nesting limit 128 exceeded" to stderr and exits 2 without panicking.
        Verified by: tests/cli_limits.rs::rejects_nesting_beyond_limit
```

## Non-goals (P §3)

List what a reasonable reader would otherwise assume is included. Leave out absurd exclusions. Non-goals
are the main defence against scope creep, so treat them as load-bearing.

## Splitting (K §6.4, §8.3)

Split vertically, so each slice produces an outcome someone can validate:

- One user journey before another.
- The read path before the write path, when the read path is useful on its own.
- One protocol operation or endpoint at a time.
- One consumer migration at a time.
- Behind a disabled flag first, then enablement.
- Core behavior before performance hardening, when the initial behavior is safe.

Never split only by technical layer (database, backend, interface). If an item cannot be split, keep the
parent outcome, track the children, and say why it needs more frequent review.

## Discovery cards (K §8.4)

A discovery card needs:

- The question or decision to resolve.
- A timebox or stopping condition.
- The evidence required.
- The candidate options and constraints.
- The expected artifact: a prototype, a benchmark, a threat model, an ADR, or a recommendation.
- An explicit statement that production implementation is not included.

## Class of service (K §7)

| Class | Only when | Card must show |
|---|---|---|
| Standard | Most work | Nothing extra |
| Fixed date | Missing the date has a material consequence | The date, the consequence, and the latest responsible start |
| Expedite | Immediate, severe cost of delay: an active incident, exploited vulnerability, severe outage, or binding emergency | Why it qualifies. WIP is one, displaced work is named, and a review follows |
| Intangible | The benefit is real but its cost of delay is not yet visible | The expected risk reduction or capability gain |

## Route

Propose `full`, `light`, `discovery`, or `expedite`, as the orchestration section of
`CLAUDE.md` defines them. A `light` proposal lists every escalation trigger and says why each
one does not apply. When unsure, choose `full`. Escalation costs one extra stage. A missed trigger costs a
design defect found in review.

## Brief gates (P §2)

List the brief sections this item depends on. For each one that is unanswered, write one of these, and
never a guessed answer:

- `not yet; needed by <stage>`
- A discovery card, with its ID.
- An assumption in force, with an owner and the cost of being wrong.

Add brief §8 and §15 as soon as the item touches data that belongs to someone.

## Definition of Ready

Copy the checklist from `docs/workflow-policy.md` into the handoff entry. Mark each line satisfied, with
the place that satisfies it, or open, with the reason and owner. Stack changes also need the S §25.2
lines. Readiness prevents obvious churn. It is not a specification gate (K §5.1).
